note: Two programs reached MDS trials: vadastuximab (PBD ADC, higher-risk MDS, stopped for portfolio reasons after a 2016 hepatotoxicity hold and the 2017 CASCADE AML halt for excess deaths) and BI 836858 (naked Fc-engineered antibody, lower-risk MDS, stopped for no hematologic response); gemtuzumab supplies the class's VOD comparison.
label: MDS (CD33-directed)

engagement.model: Primary MDS marrow ex vivo (NK ADCC)
engagement.note: BI 836858 depleted CD33+ MDSC by NK-cell ADCC in MDS patient marrow and lowered CD33 surface density ex vivo.
engagement.quote: We observed that BI 836858 can reduce MDSC by antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), which correlated with increases in granule mobilization and cell death.
engagement.judgement: The lower-risk MDS trial (NCT02240706) opened January 2015, before this paper; 2017 is the earliest published use of the model found.

engagement.model: Primary MDS marrow ex vivo (NK ADCC)
engagement.note: In 27 lower-risk MDS patients CD33 fell on MDSC but MDSC numbers and NK activation did not change: masking or internalisation, not depletion.
engagement.quote: Nevertheless, in contrast to preclinical findings, pharmacodynamic analyses indicated that BI 835858 did not activate NK cells or reduce overall MDSC numbers in patients, despite a decrease in CD33 expression.
engagement.judgement: The authors state the comparison themselves ('in contrast to preclinical findings'); full text read via PMC. The paper's own typo 'BI 835858' is kept verbatim.

dose.note: Vadastuximab's xenografts ranked its potency against gemtuzumab; no exposure or occupancy target for MDS was published.
dose.short: Xenografts rank potency, no dose target
dose.quote: In preclinical testing, SGN-CD33A is more potent than GO against a panel of AML cell lines and primary AML cells in vitro and in xenotransplantation studies in mice.
dose.judgement: Abstract-level reading; the Blood full text is paywalled.

dose.note: Higher-risk MDS phase 1 with azacitidine (19 patients) ended without a recommended dose; BI 836858's MDS trial calculated no PK parameters.
dose.quote: A recommended dose of vadastuximab talirine was not identified in Phase 1 due to study termination.
dose.reason: No dose ever fixed in MDS
dose.judgement: Registry results record is the only patient-side source for vadastuximab in MDS; the trial stopped for 'portfolio prioritization' after the 2016 hepatotoxicity hold and the CASCADE (AML) deaths, not for an MDS finding. A second untested entry is kept because it records the attempted test.

efficacy.note: Gemtuzumab's pivotal model; the class then entered high-risk MDS trials (Estey 2002) with no MDS-specific model.
efficacy.short: HL-60 xenografts cured, no MDS model
efficacy.quote: Doses of gem-ozo as low as 50 microg cal/kg given three times to mice bearing HL-60 xenografts routinely resulted in long-term, tumor-free survivors, while a nonbinding control conjugate was relatively inactive.
efficacy.judgement: Gemtuzumab is the class's approved member and was used in high-risk MDS trials, so its model opens the strip; earlier P67.6-calicheamicin work (Hinman 1993) was not verified. Abstract-level reading.

efficacy.model: Primary MDS marrow ex vivo (colony assay)
efficacy.note: BI 836858 raised CFU-GM and BFU-E colonies from 10 MDS marrows ex vivo, the first MDS-specific model for the class.
efficacy.short: MDS marrow colonies restored ex vivo
efficacy.quote: BI 836858 can also block CD33 downstream signaling preventing immune-suppressive cytokine secretion, which correlates with a significant increase in the formation of CFU-GM and BFU-E colonies.
efficacy.judgement: Kept as a second untested entry because the model changes here (an MDS-specific ex vivo model replaces AML xenografts); the status does not.

efficacy.model: Primary MDS marrow ex vivo (colony assay)
efficacy.note: No objective response, hematologic improvement or transfusion independence in 27 lower-risk MDS patients at up to 320 mg; sponsor stopped for lack of efficacy.
efficacy.quote: These data do not support the proposed mode of action and are in line with the absence of clinical activity found in the study.
efficacy.judgement: Called contra although the authors also write that no conclusions on efficacy could be drawn because of premature termination: 27 patients were dosed for a median of five cycles with zero IWG responses, and the paper itself ties the null result to the failed mechanism. A stricter reader could keep this untested. Vadastuximab's higher-risk MDS trial never reached an efficacy readout, so the ADC arm stays untested.

safety.model: Rat and cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology
safety.note: Gemtuzumab's rat/monkey toxicology lists reproductive and preneoplastic liver findings, no sinusoidal injury; VOD then appeared in AML/MDS patients (Giles 2002).
safety.quote: Additional effects in male reproductive organs occurred in repeat-dose toxicology studies and included effects on mammary gland, testes, and epididymides in rats at 2.4 mg/m2/week and effects on testes and epididymides in monkeys at 21.6 mg/m2/week.
safety.judgement: Year set to the 2000 approval, when this toxicology package was filed; the quoted text is the 2017 relabel and the original 2000 pharmacology review was not read, so the filing year is inferred, not read.

safety.note: Monkeys given a calicheamicin conjugate at 6 mg/m2 developed sinusoidal endothelial loss and early SOS, matching the VOD seen with gemtuzumab.
safety.short: Monkey liver lesion matches patient VOD
safety.quote: Liver histopathology on day 63 showed variable endothelial recovery and progression to a combination of sinusoidal capillarization and sinusoidal dilation/hepatocellular atrophy, consistent with early SOS.
safety.judgement: Retrospective: Pfizer ran the monkey study after SOS was known in gemtuzumab/inotuzumab patients, using a non-binding conjugate (PF-0259) with the same linker-payload, so it reproduces rather than predicts, and the patient side is AML/ALL rather than MDS (gemtuzumab VOD in an AML/MDS phase 1: Giles 2002). A stricter reader keeps safety untested. Vadastuximab's 2016 hepatotoxicity hold and the CASCADE deaths (AML, fatal infections) were never compared with any model; its MDS trial ended for portfolio reasons. Abstract-level reading.
